title: Fast 4-bit KV-Cache Decoding on Hopper GPUs: Why Existing Kernels Are Slow and How to Fix Them
abstract: arXiv:2611.30027v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A 4-bit KV cache reads about half the bytes of FP8, but Hopper GPUs have no FP4 hardware and little instruction-issue capacity per byte of memory bandwidth, so 4-bit values must be decoded in software. On H200, vLLM's NVFP4 KV path (FlashInfer's decode) reaches 10-20% of memory bandwidth and is up to 1.7x slower than FP8. NVBit instruction counts show two causes: the kernels behind vLLM's 4-bit paths (FlashInfer NVFP4, Triton UltraQuant) execute 2-6x Hopper's issue budget per byte and serialize loading, decoding and matrix multiplies. Our Hopper-native decode kernel overlaps a TMA producer warp with two compute warpgroups, lays the cache out at write time so decoded values feed the tensor cores from registers, and swaps the matrix operands so small query groups need no padding. On H200 it reaches 67-75% of peak bandwidth at batch 32-128 and at all 11 shapes is 1.12-1.49x faster than the faster of XQA and FlashAttention-4's proposed nativ

translated_title: Hopper GPU 上的快速 4 位 KV 缓存解码：现有内核为何慢以及如何修复
translated_abstract: 4 位 KV 缓存读取的字节数约为 FP8 的一半，但 Hopper GPU 缺乏 FP4 硬件支持，且每字节内存带宽对应的指令发射能力有限，因此 4 位数值必须通过软件进行解码。在 H200 上，vLLM 的 NVFP4 KV 路径（FlashInfer 的解码内核）仅能达到内存带宽的 10-20%，且比 FP8 慢最多 1.7 倍。NVBit 指令计数分析揭示了两个原因：vLLM 4 位路径背后的内核（FlashInfer NVFP4、Triton UltraQuant）每字节执行的指令数达到 Hopper 发射预算的 2-6 倍，并将加载、解码和矩阵乘法操作串行化。我们提出的 Hopper 原生解码内核将一个 TMA 生产者 warp 与两个计算 warpgroup 重叠执行，在写入时对缓存进行布局，使解码后的数值直接从寄存器送入张量核心，并通过交换矩阵操作数使小规模查询组无需填充。在 H200 上，批量大小为 32-128 时达到峰值带宽的 67-75%，在全部 11 种形状上比 XQA 与 FlashAttention-4 提议的原生 FP4 内核中更快者还要快 1.12-1.49 倍。
tldr: 论文针对 Hopper GPU 缺乏 FP4 硬件导致现有 4 位 KV 缓存解码内核内存带宽利用率低的问题，提出通过 TMA 生产者 warp 与计算 warpgroup 重叠、写入时缓存布局优化和矩阵操作数交换的 Hopper 原生解码内核，达到峰值带宽的 67-75%，并比现有最快内核快 1.12-1.49 倍。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Hopper-native 4-bit KV-cache decode kernel that overlaps a TMA producer warp with compute warpgroups, optimizes cache layout at write time, and swaps matrix operands, achieving 67-75% of peak bandwidth and a 1.12-1.49x speedup over the fastest existing kernels.
